questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Azerbaijan about 86,600 square kilometres; Denmark about 42,925 square kilometres; Bahrain about 787 square kilometres; Tonga about 749 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Azerbaijan?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.proof: Azerbaijan's currency is the Azerbaijani manat (AZN) which is divided into 100 qəpik.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Baku?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Azerbaijan is Baku.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Azerbaijan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Azerbaijan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Azerbaijan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.proof: It borders on Russia in the north, Georgia and, Armenia in the west, Iran in the south, and the Caspian Sea on the east.
